invariants.source: docs/DESIGN-GATE.md:219 - A citation nobody can open is not evidence, whatever it claims. The rows it guards are INDEX rows, so every decisions.md:<line> and DESIGN-GATE.md:<line> in the tree is POSITIONAL: inserting a row above one silently invalidates every citation below it, and nothing about the edited row is itself wrong.

docs/DESIGN-GATE.md:219 - A citation nobody can open is not evidence, whatever it claims. `decision-citations` proves the target EXISTS; this proves it still SAYS what the citing sentence attributes to it. Those are different failures and one does not imply the other: inserting a row above a cited one leaves every citation below it openable and pointing at the wrong line, and three citations here once asserted 'the clock's decisions.md row exists' while resolving to a blank line. The guard fingerprints the cited line's CONTENT rather than its number, so a shift reds even where the renumbering is harmless.
